notes: v276 — SPARK-QUOTA: TELEMETRY-COALESCE + RECORD-SAVE-TARGETED-READS (Oct 27, 2026, shipped as webVersion 276). Owner rule (Tue Oct 27, 2026 11:02 MDT): no paid plan until the first paying user exists — Firebase stays on the FREE Spark plan, so the app must stop burning the free quota. The Oct 27 stress test proved the app and Firestore hold under concurrency; what breaks first is Spark's daily quotas (20,000 writes/day, 50,000 reads/day project-wide), and the burn is the app's own sync: (1) the telemetry keys (livemiles, geoloads) are rewritten by their engines at most every ~10 s all shift and the sync pushed them on nearly every cycle — ~3,000–7,000 Firestore writes per driver-day, so the write cap lasted only ~4–6 active drivers; (2) every record-list save re-read the whole ~36-doc kv tree to find the one doc it merges — 36 reads per save. FIX 1 — TELEMETRY COALESCE (js/cloudsync.js): telemetry keys now push at most once per TELEMETRY_PUSH_MIN_MS = 60,000 ms per key, however often the engines persist locally (local persistence unchanged; only the cloud write cadence changes). The gate lifts at once (an URGENT flush) on tracker pause/stop — every stop, day close and dispatch close funnels through stopSessionAt, which stamps the tracker 'paused'/'idle', and the wrapped store.set raises the urgent flag on those stamps — plus page hide and beforeunload (flushUrgent). A telemetry tombstone is never gated. The coalesce clock lives at the sync-meta top level (m.teleTp) because the pull replaces whole per-key records (a per-key clock was wiped by a pull mid-shift in the first harness run — a 52.5 s gap). UNCHANGED and pinned by harness: cold-start restore of live miles, the MILES-DISPATCH-GATE, the v271 phantom identity guard + tombstone rule, the v272 union + per-key shadow semantics, the single trackerElapsedSec() derivation; durable keys push immediately as before. FIX 2 — TARGETED READS (js/firebase.js + js/cloudsync.js): new FB.loadDoc(collection, id) reads exactly one document; the record-list push's read-merge-write now reads only the doc it merges (loadCloudDoc) instead of the whole kv collection, with the loadDocs fallback standing for a half-updated bundle mid-OTA; a failed read still fails the push honestly (v272 law). HARNESS: NEW tools/spark-quota-v276-test.js — RED on the pristine v275 tree for exactly the right reasons (13 passed / 3 failed: telemetry pushes 7,022 over a simulated 10 h shift vs the ≤1,250 bound; push gaps of 10 s vs the ~55 s floor; one record save = 36 reads vs the ≤2 bound). GREEN 16/16 on the fixed tree: telemetry writes 7,022 → 1,176 over the simulated shift (~6× — the honest figure; a full ~10× would need a ~100 s gate), push gaps exactly 60 s, one record save = 1 read, cold-start restore of final totals intact, tombstone inside the gate window deletes at once, fallback merge identical. REGRESSIONS: full-sweep A/B, 198 suites on both trees — the ONLY delta is the new suite (13/3 → 16/16); every other suite identical, cloudsync family green (v136 51/51, merge 14/14, record-union-v241 14/14, damage-union-v243 6/6, fuel-history-recurrence-v272 16/16, phantom-converge-v271 19/19); standing baselines unchanged (connect-live 84/85, connect-pipe 75/77). NEW SPARK SURVIVAL: telemetry writes per driver-day ~7,200 → ~1,200; total ≈1,300–1,500 writes/driver-day → the 20,000/day write quota now lasts ~13–15 active drivers/day (was ~3–6). PIN MOVES (cited): index.html js/firebase.js 269 → 276, js/cloudsync.js 272 → 276; version.json hashes refreshed by build-ota. NAMED, NOT BUILT: WATCHDOG-PULL-READ-BURN (the 30 s watchdog pull re-reads the whole tree ~once a minute all shift, ≈21,600 reads/driver-day — the next read-quota wall); HOSTING-TRANSFER-CAP (Spark 360 MB/day — a plan wall); AI-CAP-4 and NAV-THROUGHPUT (out of scope); the Blaze upgrade stays blocked by the owner's rule until the first paying user. VERDICT OWED IN HIS HANDS: a normal work day — live miles and load counts behave exactly as before on the phone, final totals survive a cold start, records/fuel/PTI saves feel no different.
